change: Require one upper-layer NCCLCommHandle; remove Gloo and all Context bootstrap backend selectors.

variants.control: Historical EP-Xpress with the existing SGLang EP CPU bootstrap group. Its upper-layer helper was normalized to the same PyTorch EP device-group NCCL handle as the candidate. This is an initialization ablation, not the SGLang NCCL payload baseline.
variants.candidate: Context accepts only NCCLCommHandle. SGLang always supplies the existing EP device-group handle. No internal process-group creation, CPU bootstrap group, or PyNccl fallback. Host-SM token transport is unchanged.

data_plane_check.note: Only constructor, bootstrap wrappers, teardown, and upstream adapter resolution changed in the host-SM runtime.

method.production_timing: HTTP client TTFT and aggregate steady-state decode output tokens/s; unchanged normal dynamic admission.
method.aligned_timing: Scheduler-only pause admits all requests first, then the existing continue endpoint releases execution. Release-to-first-token timing excludes deliberate admission holding time. It is a diagnostic metric, not normal production TTFT.
method.first_wave_control: A private scheduler hook limits only the first prefill admission; the normal scheduler handles subsequent waves and all DP/EP synchronization. No model routes, experts, or communication kernels are replaced.
method.routing: Actual model router runs on every forward with seeded real model inputs. Per-rank input hashes and actual prefill request membership match across variants for all controlled cases; expert routes are neither cached nor prescribed.
method.event_timing: ModelRunner CUDA events resolve at the next idle flush, outside measured forwards. Event spans include compute, communication, and CPU enqueue gaps; they are not isolated communication/kernel durations.
method.cpu_probe: Second session of each variant records process CPU time, context switches, and GC callbacks outside the library.

free32.note: Five additional freely admitted diagnostic repeats per session; batch membership is observed rather than aligned.

method.aggregation: Arithmetic means; all samples from all four completed sessions retained, including the CPU submission outlier. Ranges are observed extrema, not confidence intervals.

verification.gpu_exclusivity: No external GPU process observed with two-second sampling; sub-period jobs or CPU-only interference cannot be excluded.
verification.numa: All producer arenas on configured producer NUMA nodes before and after every completed session.
verification.transports: NCCL SHM observed; no P2P, NET, or NVLS transports; all available NVLink payload counter deltas zero.
verification.greedy_output_checks: Four prompts matched exactly across all variants/sessions and the earlier accepted integration; common-prefix logprob absolute difference zero.

focused_checks.nccl_interface_gpu: 25 passed, 1 skipped, 22 subtests passed; non-contiguous subgroup, dynamic and empty routes, repeated contexts, Graph stage reuse, retained owner lifetime.
focused_checks.host_ce_api_smoke: Two ranks: mixed, empty, and all-empty routes and handle lifetime; metadata tag mismatch and invalid route rejected. External worker timeout remains required for missing-rank raw NCCL calls.

excluded_attempts: One private diagnostic attempt failed on an incorrect Scheduler rank attribute after normal performance measurement; omitted because final transport/placement checks did not complete.

One reference-API launcher attempt stalled resolving its standalone rendezvous hostname in an offline container; replaced with loopback static rendezvous. No timing from this check is inference performance.

findings: The large free-admission TTFT shift is not reproduced as a stable communicator regression after input/rank/prefill-batch alignment. Whole-batch B32 release-to-first-token is approximately 260.24 ms for control and 260.26 ms for candidate.

On the same candidate, splitting identical 32-request inputs into a 2-request first wave and a 30-request second wave raises mean release-to-first-token to approximately 326.24 ms. The initialization communicator remains unchanged.

Pinned SGLang overlap scheduling submits the next forward before processing the previous result. With consecutive eager prefills, about 90 ms of second-forward CPU submission delays first-wave token delivery even when the first GPU forward is already complete.
Host-SM still uses NCCL only for initialization and healthy teardown. This change introduces no per-layer NCCL metadata exchange or extra dispatch/combine synchronization.

Normal two-session decode TPS differs by less than 0.5% between initialization variants. The lower freely admitted candidate TTFT is not evidence that NCCL bootstrap accelerates the unchanged data plane.

outlier.observation: Rank 0/2 CPU submission durations increased to about 142/137 ms while other active ranks remained near 90-92 ms. All GPU participants inherited the delayed progress.
outlier.followup: Not reproduced in the second candidate session. Observed GC pauses in follow-up were at most 4.01 ms in candidate and 4.33 ms in control.
outlier.conclusion: Exact source of the one-off CPU submission pause remains unresolved; it is retained in all means. Follow-up does not establish GC as the cause.

limitations: This establishes behavior for the stated hardware, software, and workloads, not all dynamic serving traffic.
Controlled admission is diagnostic only; it is not a production scheduler modification or a benchmark-specific communication fast path.
The cause of different free-admission batch memberships across server runs is not established as an effect of bootstrap selection.
SGLang itself still owns CPU groups for framework operations; EP-Xpress no longer consumes or creates them.
Context no longer accepts group or bootstrap_group. The SGLang adapter requires ProcessGroupNCCL._comm_ptr(); other frameworks must explicitly provide a borrowed raw handle if needed.
Raw NCCL metadata calls have no PyTorch Work watchdog. The application must bound worker execution and close contexts before explicitly destroying their communicator owner.
privacy: No host addresses, credentials, deployment paths, request IDs, GPU identities, raw server logs, or organization identifiers are included.
